name: Learn billiards fundamentals
blurb: Stance, bridge, a straight stroke and cue-ball control. Beginners aim; players think about where the white ends up.
steps: Build the stance: back foot aligned with the shot line, chin low over the cue, body still.
Learn a solid bridge — open or closed — and keep the cue running through the same channel every time.
Learn the straight stroke: a smooth pendulum from the elbow, with the grip hand relaxed and no body movement. Practise the long straight pot down the spots.
Learn contact points and the ghost-ball method for aiming cut shots.
Learn cue-ball control: stun, follow and draw, by striking above, at, and below centre.
Start thinking two shots ahead, playing position rather than just potting.
tips: Gripping the cue tightly ruins the stroke. Hold it as if it were a bird.
Miscues come from off-centre strikes and unchalked tips.
Slow down. Almost all beginner misses are rushed strokes, not bad aim.
proof: You clear a full rack of your balls with deliberate position play, not luck.
